source_text: Quam uana igitur, immo desperata argumentatio eorum, qui sine dubio tergiuersatione amittendae uoluptatis optendunt nullam eius abstinentiae mentionem specialiter uel localiter in scripturis determinari, quae directo prohibeat eiusmodi conuentibus inseri seruum dei. nouam proxime defensionem suauiludii cuiusdam audiui. sol, inquit, immo ipse etiam deus de caelo spectat nec contaminatur. sane, sol et in cloacam radios suos defert nec inquinatur. utinam autem deus nulla flagitia hominum spectaret, ut omnes iudicium euaderemus. sed spectat et latrocinia, spectat et falsa et adulteria et fraudes et idololatrias et spectacula ipsa. et idcirco ergo nos non spectabimus, ne uideamur ab illo qui spectat omnia. comparas, homo, reum et iudicem, reum, qui, quia uidetur, reus est, iudicem, qui, quia uidet, iudex est. numquid ergo et extra limites circi furori studemus et extra cardines theatri impudicitiae intendimus et insolentiae extra stadium et immisericordiae extra amphitheatrum, quoniam deus etiam extra cameras et gradus et t apulias oculos habet? erramus: nusquam et numquam excusatur quod deus damnat, nusquam et nunquam licet quod semper et ubique non licet. haec est ueritatis integritas et, quae ei debetur, disciplinae plenitudo et aequalitas timoris et fides obsequii, non inmutare sententiam nec uariare iudicium. non potest aliud esse, quod uere quidem est bonum seu malum.
thought_title: God sees all, so no place or time excuses what he condemns
orientation: Tertullian is answering those who claim Scripture nowhere specifically forbids attending the shows, and he reports a recent objection that God himself looks on without being defiled.
pass_a_gloss: How empty therefore, or rather desperate, is the argument of those who without doubt by evasion of losing pleasure put forward that no mention of this abstinence is determined specially or locally in the Scriptures, which directly forbids servants of God to be joined to gatherings of this kind. I recently heard a new defense of a certain sweet game. The sun, he says, or rather even God himself from heaven looks on and is not contaminated. Certainly, the sun also sends down its rays into a sewer and is not polluted. But would that God looked at no crimes of men, so that we all might escape judgment. But he looks at robberies, he looks at falsehoods and adulteries and frauds and idolatries and the shows themselves. And therefore we will not look at them, lest we be seen by him who sees all things. You compare, man, the accused and the judge: the accused, who, because he is seen, is guilty; the judge, who, because he sees, is judge. Do we then also outside the limits of the circus pursue fury, and outside the hinges of the theater aim at shamelessness, and at insolence outside the stadium, and at mercilessness outside the amphitheater, since God also has eyes outside the vaults and steps and awnings? We are mistaken: nowhere and never is what God condemns excused, nowhere and never is what is always and everywhere not permitted, permitted. This is the integrity of truth and, what is owed to it, the fullness of discipline and the equality of fear and the faithfulness of obedience: not to change the sentence nor to vary the judgment. What is truly good or evil cannot be other than it is.

pass_b_english: How empty, then—no, how desperate—is the argument of those who, no doubt to evade losing their pleasure, claim that the Scriptures nowhere mention this abstinence specifically or locally, nowhere directly forbid a servant of God to enter gatherings of this kind. I recently heard a new defense of a certain sweet amusement. A pagan objector says, "The sun—indeed even God himself—looks on from heaven and is not contaminated." True enough: the sun sends its rays into a sewer and is not defiled. But would that God looked on no crimes of men, so that we might all escape judgment! Yet he does look on robberies, and he looks on falsehoods and adulteries and frauds and idolatries and the shows themselves. And for that reason, then, we will not watch, lest we be seen by him who watches all things.

You compare, man, the accused and the judge—the accused, who is guilty because he is seen, and the judge, who is judge because he sees. Do we then pursue fury outside the limits of the circus, and aim at shamelessness outside the hinges of the theater, and insolence outside the stadium, and mercilessness outside the amphitheater, because God has eyes even outside the vaults and the steps and the awnings? We are mistaken: nowhere and never is what God condemns excused; nowhere and never is what is always and everywhere unlawful permitted. This is the integrity of truth, and the fullness of discipline owed to it, and the equality of fear and the faithfulness of obedience: not to change the sentence nor to vary the judgment. What is truly good or evil cannot be anything other than it is.
notes: The word 't apulias' in the source appears to contain a stray 't' before 'apulias'; the gloss renders it as 'awnings' based on the context of circus coverings.

last_rejected.quote: "The sun," someone says, "indeed even God himself, looks on from heaven and is not contaminated."
last_rejected.source_quote: sol, inquit, immo ipse etiam deus de caelo spectat nec contaminatur.
last_rejected.why: The Latin has the sun speaking; English replaces the sun with an anonymous speaker, altering agency.
last_rejected.fix: "The sun," it says, "indeed even God himself looks on from heaven and is not contaminated."
last_rejected.ruling: inquit is parenthetical 'says he/she,' not 'the sun says.' Context: someone argues sun/God look unsullied; translator rightly attributes to a speaker.
